reason: E2 shows laser cladding was used to improve wear resistance of TC4 via solid solution strengthening, supporting the feasibility of the intervention and part of the mechanism. However, no cited evidence supports the specific microstructural claims (fine grains, dispersed hard phases), the quantitative hardness/wear predictions, or the retention of bulk properties. E1 discusses WC-reinforced HEA composites, not laser cladding on TC4, and is misrepresented as support.
premises: Laser cladding can deposit a metallurgically bonded, wear-resistant coating on TC4
The coating will have a refined, fine-grained microstructure with dispersed hard phases
Rapid solidification during laser cladding enables solid solution/dispersion strengthening and grain refinement
The coating will increase surface hardness by 1.5–2 times and reduce wear rate
The treatment will not degrade bulk ductility, low weight, or corrosion resistance
